clue.text: Gems on person's garment ripped in rumpy pumpy?

indicators.note: in this across clue the gems are placed on, that is after, the person

parts.note: BOD is slang for a person; the 's simply joins the pieces
ICE is slang for diamonds or other gems

explanation.surface: Jewels end up on someone's clothes torn off in a moment of passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rumpy pumpy' is British slang for sex; the definition plays on the bodice-ripper, a lusty romance novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A bodice is the close-fitting upper part of a dress, the item torn in a bodice-ripper romance.

clue.text: Nose in fight broken by that Parisian

indicators.note: the fight is split open so that the French word sits inside it

parts.note: a bout is a boxing match or fight
QUE is French for 'that'

explanation.surface: Someone's nose gets broken in a scrap with a Frenchman.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine taster's nose is the aroma of a wine, also called its bouquet.

clue.text: Number gathering on the way to enlightenment?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a do is a party or social gathering
Zen Buddhism seeks enlightenment through meditation

explanation.surface: A crowd of people meeting on the road to spiritual awakening.
explanation.definitionFit: A dozen is the number twelve.

clue.text: Regal item soldiers put on individual in court

indicators.note: the soldiers and individual go inside the court abbreviation
in a down clue the soldiers are placed on top of the individual

parts.note: OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
one means a single individual

explanation.surface: Royal regalia worn by a single person at court, guarded by troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronet is a small crown, worn by royalty and nobility.

clue.text: We're told one like Daniel returns

indicators.note: what we are told is heard, signalling a word that sounds like another

parts.note: Daniel is one of the Old Testament prophets

explanation.surface: Apparently someone resembling Daniel is coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: Returns on an investment are the profit it yields.

clue.text: Fine: yours truly cuts eggs for a starter

indicators.note: the two pieces cut into the eggs, landing inside them

parts.note: roe is fish eggs
OK means fine
yours truly is the setter, I

explanation.surface: A restaurant critic approves of a roe dish served as an appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' suggests a first course, which the eggs encourage, but it means a beginner.
explanation.definitionFit: A rookie is a newcomer or beginner, someone just starting out.

clue.text: Learner's aid in Ferrari, say, beginning to drive

parts.note: a Ferrari is an example of a flash car

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word drive is used

explanation.surface: A learner driver gets help from starting out in a Ferrari.
explanation.definitionFit: A flashcard is a card shown to students as a memory aid when learning.

clue.text: Storybooks and special gifts

parts.note: a tale is a story
NTS stands for New Testaments, books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A list of presents: children's storybooks and other special things.
explanation.walkthrough: The single printed word 'Storybooks' splits into two pieces, story and books, each giving its own letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Talents are natural abilities, often called gifts.

clue.text: Driver inclined to career as drug trafficker

definitions.meaning: taken literally, a dealer in speed, the slang name for amphetamine

explanation.surface: A boy racer moonlighting as a dealer.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed merchant is an idiom for a reckless fast driver, and speed is street slang for amphetamines.

clue.text: Ring with news in current term

parts.note: to give someone a buzz is to ring them
word means news, as in 'any word?'

explanation.surface: A phone call bringing updates, about a fashionable expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A buzzword is a fashionable piece of jargon of the moment.

clue.text: It's again demonstrable to be worthy of censure

parts.note: RE- is the prefix meaning again
provable means able to be demonstrated

explanation.surface: A case for a reprimand that can once more be shown to stand.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprove is to rebuke, so something reprovable deserves a scolding.

clue.text: How to generate no reason to get excited

parts.note: read as an instruction, TURN the word ON round and it will generate the word no

explanation.surface: A recipe for producing a refusal.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay and it makes the clue's words.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn-on is something that arouses or thrills someone.

clue.text: What detains Dickens hero before every realisation

indicators.note: the first part comes ahead of the last word
the exclamation holds the hero inside it

parts.note: 'Eh?' is a way of saying 'What?'
Pip is the hero of Dickens's Great Expectations
any can mean every, as in 'any fool knows'

explanation.surface: Puzzling over what keeps a Dickens character from a sudden insight.
explanation.definitionFit: An epiphany is a sudden moment of insight or understanding.

clue.text: Where some journalists work briefly, then

indicators.note: cut short, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: journalists at The Times newspaper work there

explanation.surface: A short note on the newsroom where some reporters are employed.
explanation.definitionFit: At the time is an idiom meaning on that occasion in the past.

clue.text: Put in dash of neat rum husband found in promotion at first

indicators.note: the husband and shuffled letters are placed inside the promotion word

parts.note: hype is excessive promotion or publicity

indicators.note: the husband comes first, ahead of the shuffled letters
rum means odd or strange, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A drinker adds a splash of neat rum, with the husband promoted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rum' signals an anagram of NEAT; the husband goes before it, and 'found in' places both inside the promotion word. 'Dash' looks like a small amount of drink but is the punctuation mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To hyphenate is to join words with a hyphen, a short dash.

clue.text: See 16
Police seizing unknown pet apes

indicators.note: the police grab the other pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: cops are police officers
Y is an unknown in algebra
a cat is a pet

explanation.surface: Officers capture a mysterious animal, along with some monkeys.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apes' looks like monkeys, but it is a noun for imitators.
explanation.definitionFit: Copycats are imitators, people who ape or mimic others.

clue.text: Toast, one round with topping of egg on

indicators.note: in this down clue the first piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: to cheer on is to egg on, encourage
I is the Roman numeral one
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A slice of toast, one round, topped with egg.
explanation.walkthrough: The breakfast picture misleads: 'egg on' is a verb meaning encourage.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheerio is a friendly drinking salutation or farewell, like cheers.

clue.text: Serious measure of drink after fun in Ireland

indicators.note: the drink word comes after the fun word

parts.note: craic, spelt crack in English, is Irish for fun and good company
to down a drink is to drink it

explanation.surface: A stiff measure of whiskey after a lively night out in Dublin.
explanation.definitionFit: A crackdown is a severe official clampdown on wrongdoing.

clue.text: Scroungers and rotters holding what's on plate up

indicators.note: the rotters hold the other letters inside

parts.note: cads are rotters, dishonourable men

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: REG is short for registration, shown on a car's number plate

explanation.surface: Freeloaders and scoundrels raising food from the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plate' looks like a dinner plate but is a car's number plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Cadgers are people who beg or sponge things from others.

clue.text: Western state ruler, one like Hamlet?

parts.note: to aver is to state firmly
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A monarch of a western land, perhaps a prince like Hamlet.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet is famously indecisive, a classic example of someone who hesitates.

clue.text: Porridge that is part of course done well

parts.note: porridge and bird are both British slang for time in prison

explanation.surface: Porridge served as one course of a meal, cooked well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a meal but is a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: A birdie is a golf hole completed one stroke under par, a good result.

clue.text: School clothing always very hot

indicators.note: the school word wraps around the other word

parts.note: a school is a group of fish
ever means always

explanation.surface: A school uniform that is always far too warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish describes someone running a high temperature.

clue.text: Fruit boxes drip in this case

indicators.note: the fruit encloses the drip letters

parts.note: a date is a fruit
IV, intravenous, is a hospital drip

explanation.surface: Fruit packed in containers alongside a medical drip.
explanation.definitionFit: The dative is a grammatical case, marking the indirect object.

clue.text: Pull on earl's coat, which is drier

parts.note: to tow is to pull

indicators.note: the coat of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A nobleman pulls on his coat to keep dry.
explanation.definitionFit: A towel is used to dry things, so it is something that dries.

clue.text: Way to get caned in funky performance

parts.note: read as wordplay, BREAK the word DANCE up and its letters make CANED

explanation.surface: A route to corporal punishment through a disreputable show.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer read as an instruction produces the clue's words.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakdancing is an energetic street dance style performed to funk and hip-hop.

clue.text: See 9
Boycott, say, Frenchman rejected after work

indicators.note: the reversed name comes after the work

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: the name is sent back, so it reads backwards

parts.note: René is a typical French man's name

explanation.surface: A boycott of a French man after a job.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott was an English cricketer who opened the batting; 'Boycott' looks like a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: An opener is a cricket batsman who starts the innings, as Boycott did.

clue.text: Stone remains, article clutched in both hands

parts.note: ash is what remains after burning

indicators.note: the article is held between the two hand letters

parts.note: L and R are left and right, both hands
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Remains of a stone, an item gripped in both hands.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashlar is dressed, squared building stone.
